title: Universal Infectious Disease Forecasting with Mantis 2
abstract: arXiv:2611.16935v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Public health agencies need to anticipate how outbreaks will unfold, when they will peak, and how long demand on health services will remain elevated. We previously developed a foundation model, Mantis, which was trained entirely on simulated outbreaks---enabling us to generate the diversity and scale of training data needed to support forecasting across diseases. However, our previous work left unresolved when simulation improves predictions and how it should complement observational data.   Here, we varied the balance of simulated and observed training data while holding forecasting tasks fixed and varying the available surveillance history. We found that simulation-rich training was particularly valuable with limited local history, and its relative advantage diminished as more observations became available. translated_title: 基于 Mantis 2 的通用传染病预测
translated_abstract: 公共卫生机构需要预测疫情将如何演变、何时达到峰值，以及医疗服务需求将在多长时间内保持高位。我们此前开发了一个基础模型 Mantis，它完全基于模拟疫情进行训练——这使我们能够生成支持跨疾病预测所需的训练数据的多样性和规模。然而，我们之前的工作尚未解决模拟在何时能改善预测，以及它应如何与观测数据互补的问题。在本文中，我们在保持预测任务固定的情况下，改变模拟数据与观测数据的训练配比，并变换可用的监测历史长度。我们发现，在本地历史数据有限的情况下，以模拟为主的训练尤其有价值，而随着观测数据的增多，其相对优势逐渐减弱。我们还发现，基于模拟的训练减少了异常大的预测误差，这表明机制性知识……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究系统探究了模拟数据与观测数据在 Mantis 2 通用传染病预测模型中的配比作用，发现在本地监测历史有限时以模拟为主的训练最有价值，且能显著减少异常大的预测误差。
en_tdlr: This study systematically examines the balance between simulated and observed training data in Mantis 2 for universal infectious disease forecasting, finding that simulation-rich training is most valuable when local surveillance history is limited and reduces exceptionally large forecast errors.
